rationale: Edge-case lens raised 4 candidates; 2 were dismissed after reading codemie_enterprise/litellm/service.py: ensure_team_exists() is a plain sync def (not a coroutine) and it already catches httpx.HTTPError/Exception internally and returns False rather than propagating, so the not-awaited and log-leaks-credentials claims do not hold. The remaining 2 (CR-001, CR-002) were real at the reviewed snapshot but were both fixed by commit 02f749d54 ('Run LiteLLM team provisioning off the startup event loop'): the call is now offloaded via `asyncio.to_thread`, and its boolean return value is checked to log a warning on a soft provisioning failure instead of always logging success. Acceptance lens confirms all 4 story ACs pass; standards review is intentionally out of scope for the compact profile, so its rows are na with no coverage gap.

business_review.item: AC1: calls ensure_team_exists() once at startup, immediately before budget-provider registration, gated on litellm_service present and LLM_PROXY_BUDGET_CHECK_ENABLED
business_review.notes: main.py:296-301 sits directly before the pre-existing budget-provider registration block, under the same two-part gate.

business_review.item: AC2: startup remains idempotent across repeated runs; duplicate-creation avoidance delegated to ensure_team_exists()
business_review.notes: try/except prevents any exception from propagating out of _initialize_enterprise_services; dedup logic lives in codemie-enterprise, out of this repo's scope.

business_review.item: AC3: if ensure_team_exists() raises, the exception is caught, a warning is logged, and budget-provider registration still proceeds
business_review.notes: try/except at main.py:297-301 logs via logger.warning and falls through to proxy/budget registration; covered by a dedicated test.

business_review.notes: Guard at main.py:296 covers both conditions; covered by two dedicated skip tests.

findings.title: Sync LiteLLM call blocks the async startup loop
findings.problem: litellm_service.ensure_team_exists() makes a blocking synchronous HTTP call (via LiteLLMAPIClient, default 5s timeout per request, two requests possible) and is invoked directly inside `async def lifespan`, which runs on the single startup event loop.
findings.impact: Every application startup now blocks the event loop for up to several seconds when the LiteLLM proxy is slow, unreachable, or under load, delaying readiness/liveness signals for that window; this is a newly introduced blocking call in an otherwise non-blocking startup path.
findings.recommendation: Offload the call, e.g. `await asyncio.to_thread(litellm_service.ensure_team_exists)`, or make `_initialize_enterprise_services` async and run the call through an executor, so the event loop is not blocked during startup.
findings.resolution: Fixed in commit 02f749d54: `_initialize_enterprise_services` is now `async def` and awaits `asyncio.to_thread(litellm_service.ensure_team_exists)`, so the blocking call no longer runs on the startup event loop.

findings.title: ensure_team_exists() return value is ignored
findings.problem: ensure_team_exists() returns False (not an exception) whenever the underlying check/create HTTP call fails, because it catches httpx.HTTPError and Exception internally; the new call site never inspects that return value and unconditionally logs "LiteLLM codemie-projects team provisioning ensured" as if it succeeded.
findings.impact: A soft provisioning failure (the far more likely failure mode, since HTTP errors are swallowed inside ensure_team_exists and rarely reach the outer try/except) is masked as a success in the logs, making a missing/unprovisioned team hard to detect operationally.
findings.recommendation: Check the boolean result and log accordingly, e.g. `if litellm_service.ensure_team_exists(): logger.info(...) else: logger.warning("LiteLLM codemie-projects team could not be confirmed/created")`.
findings.resolution: Fixed in commit 02f749d54: the call site captures `team_provisioned = await asyncio.to_thread(...)` and branches on it, logging `logger.warning("LiteLLM codemie-projects team could not be confirmed/created")` when falsy instead of unconditionally logging success. The return value carries no other business logic beyond driving this log level.
